text:
maria: customer AcmeHealth (prod-eu) reports GitHub SSO failing during login. They see a redirect to our callback but it's using a fragment, so our server gets no `code` -> 400 invalid_request. :warning:

jordan_acme: repro steps from their side: Android app opens webview -> github oauth -> redirect to `acme://auth#code=...&state=...` -> app catches fragment and calls backend `/auth/callback` with no query params.

maria: exact callback we see in logs: `GET /auth/callback` host: `app.acmehealth.com` cookies: `session=...` no `code` or `state` query. They pasted the original redirect URL they received from github: `https://app.acmehealth.com/auth/callback#code=SplITnObase64&state=xyz123`

dan: ok so GH returned a fragment rather than query. That usually means implicit flow or a client-side PKCE handling scenario. But they said they configured standard authorization_code + PKCE.

sharon: can they be using `response_type=token` or `response_mode=fragment`? Also mobile webviews sometimes transform redirect handling for deep links.

jordan_acme: I checked their mobile code. They use WebView and a deep link handler that intercepts the `acme://` scheme. The app then POSTs the fragment content to our backend at `/mobile/auth/finish` but that endpoint is not wired to exchange code -> we expect the code on the server callback.

alex: couple of quick mitigations: 1) if the mobile app can't send the code to the server, they must exchange the code from the app (not ideal), or 2) update the app to send the code to our server endpoint, or 3) change the OAuth flow to use `response_mode=form_post` so GH will POST the code to the callback instead of returning a fragment.

maria: also noticed PKCE mismatch errors in earlier attempts: when we get a code (rarely) the code_verifier doesn't match. Customer uses a custom base64 urlsafe encode that drops padding `=` which our verifier code expects. Example: their code_challenge is `abc123...` but when we recompute we see trailing `=` on our side.

dan: ah that explains intermittent 400 on exchange. RFC6749 base64url encoding *can* omit padding, but our verifier accepts both. We should log normalized verifier in debug. For now ask them to use standard urlsafe base64 without stripping padding or let us normalize.

sharon: another angle: cookies / SameSite. Their app's webview is doing a redirect from `github.com` -> `app.acmehealth.com` but also changes host via CDN `auth-eu.acmehealth-cdn.com` which rewrites query -> fragment in one of the redirect hops (we've seen bad CDN rule patterns that replace `?` with `#` in some edge rewrites). Can we ask them to check CDN rewrite rules?

jordan_acme: confirmed: their CDN has an edge rule `rewrite?to=#` (they thought it was harmless). Removing it fixed fragment during our local tests. They pushed a staging fix.

maria: next steps for us: 1) ask customer to remove CDN rewrite and re-test, 2) provide app workaround: open auth in external browser (custom tabs) instead of WebView, 3) if they can't change app, update mobile flow to POST fragment to our `/mobile/auth/finish` which will then call token endpoint with code+verifier.

alex: I'll file an internal ticket to improve our logs and tooltip: log normalized code_challenge and accept padding-omitted variants, and add a KB entry for mobile deep-link flows. @support-bot can you create the ticket?

support-bot: created TICKET-7891: "OAuth mobile deep link / fragment callback causing missing code + PKCE padding mismatch" and linked to customer AcmeHealth (prod-eu).

dan: marking this high priority - customer-facing login broken. Follow up with their engineering lead and confirm staging CDN rule removal makes login succeed.

maria: verified with jordan_acme on call — staging successful after CDN fix and app switched to custom tabs. Recommending long-term fixes on both sides. Closing once they confirm prod deploy. :thumbsup:

jordan_acme: thanks all, we'll deploy to prod tomorrow and update ticket TICKET-7891 with results.
